name: Helion Manufacturing Radiation Exposure Suit
description:
A lead-composite layered suit designed for work in environments with elevated ionizing radiation. The suit incorporates dosimetry sensors at twelve body points that provide real-time exposure tracking. When cumulative dose approaches safe limits, the suit's collar-mounted indicator changes from green to amber to red.

Used in reactor maintenance, medical imaging equipment servicing, and the cleanup of sites where radioactive materials have been improperly stored or dumped — which in GLMZ's lower tiers happens more often than any authority acknowledges.
functionality: Ionizing radiation shielding, real-time dose tracking, exposure limit warnings
what_it_says: You work near things that damage your DNA and this suit is the only reason your cells are still copying correctly.
story_hooks: A Radiation Exposure Suit's dosimetry logs show a worker was exposed to a radiation source that doesn't match anything at their assigned work site — something radioactive was there that wasn't supposed to be.

physical_description.visual_profile: A utilitarian full-body suit with a distinctly industrial silhouette. The garment reads as purpose-built rather than fashionable—broad shoulders, reinforced torso, and a subtle shimmer from embedded lead-composite weave. The collar features a prominent indicator strip that dominates the neckline. Worn by Tier 3-5 workers in contaminated zones, it signals expertise and exposure to danger.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the shoulders and torso to accommodate layered undergarments and movement in tight reactor spaces. Tapered at the wrists and ankles with friction-fit cuffs that seal against gloves and booties. The cut prioritizes functional range of motion over aesthetics.
physical_description.primary_material: Lead-composite ballistic weave—a dense synthetic blend woven with lead-infused filaments. Treated for flexibility despite its shielding properties. The outer surface is a matte grey-silver with subtle reflective qualities.
physical_description.texture: Smooth but slightly stiff to the touch, with a faint quilted texture from internal shielding layers. Micro-ridged sections at high-stress joints for grip and durability. The collar indicator strip feels rubberized and slightly raised.
physical_description.color_scheme: Industrial grey-silver base with twelve small circular dosimetry sensor nodes in matte black scattered across the body (shoulders, upper back, chest, forearms, hips, thighs, shins). The collar indicator strip transitions from safety-green to amber to warning-red depending on exposure level.
physical_description.closures: Heavy-duty magnetic snaps running down the front center, spaced 4 inches apart for quick removal in emergency situations. Reinforced friction-fit seals at wrists and ankles. No traditional zipper—the snaps allow full front opening for rapid decontamination.
distinctive_features: Twelve integrated biosensor nodes with subtle LED indicators
Collar-mounted tri-color dosimetry indicator (green/amber/red) that's visible from distance
Internal lead-composite layering visible at torn edges or seams (silver-grey glint)
Reinforced double-stitching along all seams in contrasting dark thread
Subtle Helion Manufacturing etched logo on right shoulder
Decontamination-resistant treated surface (water and particulate runoff)
Internal soft-flex lining to reduce chafing during extended wear
Small utility loops at hips for clip-on dosimetry monitors or emergency tools
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 3-4 functional. Expensive enough to signal legitimate industrial employment, but the suit's worn appearance in lower-tier zones indicates users operating in poorly-regulated contamination sites for Tier 5 salvage wages.
physical_description.cultural_context: Worn by reactor technicians, medical imaging technicians, hazmat cleanup workers, and the growing population of unregistered 'rad-scavengers' in GLMZ's ungoverned zones. Signals either corpo-aligned technical expertise or desperation-driven survival work in contaminated sectors. The red indicator is a badge of accumulated risk.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in and weathered. Users accumulate faint discoloration patterns from repeated decontamination sprays. Sensor nodes may show scuffing. The suit is rarely pristine—it's a tool that absorbs the evidence of its use.
